The Present Perfect Tense with Past Tenses
You can use the Present Perfect tense to:

1. talk about states or events that started in the past and continue to now. You can refer to these events with the words since or ever since.

For example:

She's been better behaved since she had that warning.
Ever since I met you, I've felt so much better about things.

2. describe repeated or long-term feelings or thoughts about past events.

For example:

I've often wondered why they decided to promote Rhonda.
I've always felt we did the right when we hired her.
Ever since we met Ms. Moore, I've had the same impression.
Mr. Brody has also been very interested in my ideas for new books and articles every time to spoke to him.
I've learned to organize the steps and calculate expenditures of a project in the courses I took.
The Future Continuous and Future Perfect Tenses
You can use a variety of tenses to talk about the future. Let's compare the Future Continuous and Future Perfect tenses.
Look at the chart for an outline of the meanings/uses and the form of the Future Continuous and Future Perfect tenses.

images.text:
Adam: Ouff! We've made it to lunchtime!
Kristi: We've received a lot of information since we started this morning! By the end of the day, we will have met almost everybody in the office.
Adam: Yeah, tell me about it. The company seems very well organized.
Kristi: Absolutely. Can we go over our new responsibilities? Ms. Moore talked about that briefly.
Adam: I think we will be doing more editing and revision work than original writing. At least, that's true while we are under probation.
Kristi: I think you're right. Ever since we met Ms. Moore, I've had the same impression.

Adam: We think we will be proofreading texts while we check for the accuracy of factual information. As soon as illustrations are needed, I expect we will be researching for images, or making arrangements with photographers or illustrators.
Kristi: Then there's the aspect of project management. That seems interesting, too. I've learned to organize the steps and calculate expenditures of a project in the courses I took. They said we would be liaising with authors, marketing staff, designers and printers at each stage of the process. I hope we will be learning more about how to deal with copyright issues, like researching titles to make sure they have not been used already.

Adam: Ms. Moore mentioned something about commissioning articles and recruiting authors. Have you been listening to everything she said?
Kristi: Not really. We'll have to ask. I hope we will be given the chance to propose some of our original writing.
Adam: Mr. Brody has also been very interested in my ideas for new books and articles every time to spoke to him. I have a lot of ideas to share as soon as we have settled in to our new roles.
